transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

The most common cause is a build-up of detergent/softener residue and bacteria in the drawer, rubber door seal and outer drum. It can make freshly washed clothes smell musty even though the machine appears to wash normally. Poor spinning/draining, leaving washing in the drum, or putting a full wash load straight into a dry cycle can also leave laundry damp enough to smell. Try this first: clean the detergent drawer and the folds of the door seal, then run an empty hot 60–90°C maintenance wash with a proper washing-machine cleaner (not washing in it). Afterwards, with the machine switched off and unplugged, clean the pump filter at the lower front: put towels and a shallow tray down, as water may come out. For future washes, use less detergent and fabric conditioner, avoid very low-temperature washes all the time, and take the load out promptly. If the filter is clear and an empty hot clean does not cure it, the key question is whether clothes come out properly spun/dry enough after washing, or are still noticeably wet.
ok thanks, will try that. clothes come out spun fine, not wet, just smelly. do i need a special cleaner for the hot wash or is there something else i can use?

A proper washing-machine cleaner is the best option: use it exactly as the packet directs in an empty hot 60–90°C cycle. You do not need a Samsung-specific one. If you cannot get one, washing soda can help shift detergent residue, but avoid using washing-up liquid, bleach mixed with anything else, or vinegar together with other cleaners; these can foam, damage components or create fumes. As the clothes are spinning dry, this is much more likely to be residue/bacteria in the drawer, seal, drum or filter than a spin fault. After the hot clean, with the machine switched off and unplugged, check and clean the pump filter with towels and a shallow tray ready for water. If the smell still persists after that, especially if it smells like drains rather than mildew, the drain hose/waste connection may be contributing.
ok great, i'll get some proper cleaner then. the smell isnt like drains btw, more like damp mildew. anything else i should do or is that it?

That should usually be enough, but two habits make the difference afterwards: leave the door and detergent drawer slightly open between washes so the machine can dry out, and use the detergent/conditioner dose for your water hardness and load size rather than filling the drawer. Also clean the drawer housing itself, not just the removable drawer—residue often sits in the roof and corners of that recess. With the machine switched off and unplugged, check the door-seal folds for embedded black mould or a split/perished area that can hold it; a badly mould-stained or damaged seal may need an engineer to replace it if cleaning does not shift the smell. A hot maintenance wash every month or so, especially if most washes are cool, should prevent it returning.

candidates: Build-up of detergent, softener residue and bacteria in the drum, drawer or door seal (high)
Laundry left damp because of poor draining/spinning or an overloaded wash (medium)
Drying load too large or drying cycle not fully drying the load (medium)
